articleBody:
Planning a new island is exciting, but jumping straight into stone colors without checking logistics often leads to regrets. Use this practical preparation checklist before locking in your cabinet order.

- [ ] Measure surrounding aisle widths — Keeping 36 to 42 inches of open floor space prevents pinch points between opposing cabinet runs.
- [ ] Confirm electrical outlet requirements — Building codes routinely require dedicated island receptacles, which means running wires beneath the existing finished flooring.
- [ ] Inspect subfloor level and framing — Heavy stone countertops require a flat, rigid base so cabinet boxes do not twist or crack over time.
- [ ] Check seating overhang depth — Counter stools generally need 12 to 15 inches of clear knee space supported by hidden steel brackets.
- [ ] Review appliance door clearance — Ensure refrigerator, dishwasher, and oven doors can swing fully open without hitting the new island edge.
- [ ] Coordinate plumbing vent pathways — Island sinks cannot vent straight up through walls, requiring specialized loop or air admittance valve planning.
- [ ] Select moisture-resistant base materials — Islands endure spills, wet mops, and dropped items, making durable cabinet finishes essential.
- [ ] Verify circuit capacity in your panel — Adding garbage disposals, dishwashers, or microwave drawers requires enough breaker space in your main service panel.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through your kitchen with a tape measure and review these points before meeting with your designer or builder. Knowing your structural boundaries early saves real time and keeps budgets steady.
